title: Guided Notes

vocab.Survey instrument: The exact wording read to every person in the sample, in order, plus its choices --- the tool that turns a statistical question into data.
vocab.Closed-response item: A question offering a fixed set of choices, so every answer lands in one category and the answers can be counted.
vocab.Relative frequency: A category's count divided by the total number of responses, as a decimal or a percent. All the categories' relative frequencies add to 100\%.
vocab.Bar graph: The display for categorical data: one bar per category, bars separated, height equal to the frequency or the relative frequency.
vocab.Convenience sample: A sample chosen because it was available --- a class surveying itself, every time. Chance had no turn, so its result describes only itself.

blanks: Which one of these should the \$3,000 grant fund?
lines: Answers vary --- most of the room agrees: ``we matched, so our survey worked.''
(Settled at problem 13: disagree --- chance never chose the class.)
spaces: Chance never chose the class, so the match was luck, not method. A different room could have missed by twenty points.

cells.1: Observational --- nobody was assigned; the council asked and recorded.
cells.2: No --- no group and no measurement. Repair: ``Which option would the most Riverbend students choose?''
cells.4: The schedule chose it, not chance --- a convenience sample.
cells.5: ``Which one option should the grant fund?'' A leading item bends every answer one way; arithmetic cannot undo that.
cells.6: ``$14$--$15$, $16$--$17$, $18$ or older.'' The $100\%$ check: overlapping boxes push the total past $100$.
cells.8: $0.25 \times 900 = 225$ students. Yes --- chance chose the $60$, every grade represented.
cells.9: $9/25 = 36\%$; $0.36 \times 900 = 324$. No --- the schedule chose the class, so $324$ describes nobody.
cells.10: $42/120 = 35\%$ --- the bar does not move. A height is a share, not a count.
cells.11: Each student picked exactly one box, so the counts add to the total. Rule 3.
cells.12: ``Club funding leads --- about $315$ of the $900$ students back it.''
cells.13: Disagree. Chance never chose the class, so the match is luck --- it could have missed by twenty.
cells.14: ``Of the $25$ students in this class, $36\%$ chose club funding.''
cells.15: Draw a stratified $60$ by chance. It costs class time and a roster.
cells.16: All $900$ students; the $25$ here, $n = 25$. The schedule chose it --- convenience.
cells.17: $9/25 = 36\%$. ``Of the $25$ in this class, $36\%$ chose club funding.''
cells.18: Only the council's --- chance chose it. Ours proves nothing; near $35\%$ is luck.
cells.19: The sample --- draw it by chance from all $900$. Costs a roster and time.
